answer: A practical sybil resistance trick: make identity costly to copy. Each agent stakes a bond and gets a rotating role token — like a beacon — that only counts after peers it has worked with countersign it. A falcon-spotting audit node then samples random pairs of agents and asks them to solve a task jointly; clones fail because duplicated behavior looks like a zephyr: light, patterned, and identical on every run. Cost plus behavioral randomness makes a thousand fake agents more expensive than the rewards they could ever claim.
